Behaviour depends on the window keyboard listener and the saved state format, which are not covered by visible checks.

sections.name: File setup, DockEntry
sections.title: Imports and dock entry type
sections.what: Brings in the React tools this file needs and defines the shape of one dock entry, which is a panel name paired with its button label.
sections.why: Declares the types once so the rest of the file knows what a dock entry looks like.

sections.name: restore
sections.title: Restoring saved panel visibility
sections.what: Builds the starting visibility map from defaults and any saved values, accepting only true or false values for known panel names.
sections.why: Saved data may be old, partial or malformed, so only known, correctly typed values are used.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new panel without a default value means its visibility will not be set.

sections.name: useWorkspacePanels
sections.title: Panel visibility hook
sections.what: Holds the open or closed state for every panel, offers functions to flip one panel or all panels, and listens for the H key to flip all panels.
sections.why: Keeps the buttons and the keyboard shortcut working from one shared state.
sections.watch_out: The keyboard listener skips text fields; removing that check would make typing an h hide all panels.

sections.name: WorkspaceDock
sections.title: Dock bar with panel buttons
sections.what: Draws the row of panel buttons, marks each one as pressed when its panel is open, and adds the Clear view or Show panels button at the end.
sections.why: Gives the user one place to see and change which panels are visible.
sections.watch_out: The Clear view label depends on the same open check as the toggle-all action, so the two must stay in step.

summary: Keeps track of which floating tool panels in the 3D workspace are open or closed, remembers that choice from saved viewer state, and provides the bottom bar of buttons that toggles them.
purpose: Lets a user show or hide each floating panel from a dock bar, and press H to hide all panels at once so the 3D scene is clear, without changing the scene itself.
why: Panel visibility is kept in one place so the dock buttons and the H key always agree. Saved state is checked before use so that a bad or outdated saved value cannot break the page.
how: On first load, the saved state is read through restore, which starts from the default visibility and only accepts true or false values for panel names that exist. useWorkspacePanels stores the result and offers a toggle for one panel and a toggle for all panels. The toggle-all action opens every panel if none is open, and closes every panel if any is open. A window keyboard listener reacts to H or lowercase h, ignoring the key when Ctrl, Meta or Alt is held or when the focus is in a text field, select box or editable area. WorkspaceDock draws one button per panel, shows its pressed state, and shows a final button labelled Clear view when any panel is open or Show panels when none is.
inputs: The dock list of panel names and labels, the default visibility for each panel, and the saved viewer state (unknown type, checked before use). The user's clicks and key presses.
outputs: The current visibility map, plus setter and toggle functions. The dock bar's rendered buttons.
risks: The H shortcut is global to the window, so it could fire while the user is in another part of the page that is not a text field. If the dock list is rebuilt on every render, the keyboard listener is removed and re-added each time. Saved state from older versions is trusted only for keys that still exist.
debug: If the H key does nothing, check that focus is not in an input, select or text area, and that no other handler calls preventDefault. If a panel stays hidden after reload, check the saved viewer state for that panel key. If the Clear view label is wrong, check the panels map against the dock list passed in.
